description: VinSpace10 is a four-member team of student developers passionate about space, game development, and building useful technology. Our strengths include full-stack development, interactive simulations, UI/UX, and AI integration. We aim to turn NASA data into a creative, scientifically grounded project with a polished demo. We welcome collaborators with skills in planetary science, GIS, data visualization, 3D design, or scientific storytelling.
summary:
MARS NAVIGATOR - Explore Smarter. Survive Longer

How can astronauts navigate an unfamiliar planet where every route involves trade-offs between distance, terrain difficulty, and limited resources?
MARS NAVIGATOR is an interactive Mars exploration and navigation prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Addressing the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge, our project transforms real Mars terrain data into an accessible route-planning and exploration experience.
Using imagery and elevation data from NASA-supported Mars missions and USGS planetary mapping products, our platform combines an interactive map, terrain visualization, and an A* pathfinding algorithm. Users can compare two routes: Shortest, which prioritizes distance, and Terrain-aware, which considers modeled terrain difficulty.
The experience extends into a 3D astronaut expedition simulation where users navigate Martian terrain, manage simulated oxygen and energy, and complete exploration objectives.
Our goal is to make planetary navigation more understandable, engaging, and accessible while demonstrating how open scientific data can support future exploration planning, education, and research.
details:
MARS NAVIGATOR - Project Details

1. What Does Our Project Do?

MARS NAVIGATOR is a web-based Mars navigation and exploration prototype that combines real planetary terrain data, route planning, and interactive 3D simulation.

Our project focuses on the western fan region of Jezero Crater, a scientifically significant area explored by NASA's Perseverance rover.

The platform provides:

  • Interactive Mars Map: Explore a terrain map derived from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Context Camera (CTX) imagery.
  • Dual Route Planning: Compare the Shortest route with a Terrain-aware route that accounts for modeled surface difficulty.
  • Terrain Analysis: Visualize elevation, slope-related hazards, and restricted navigation areas.
  • 3D Astronaut Expedition: Explore a simulated Martian environment using a 3D terrain surface derived from elevation data.
  • Mission Simulation: Navigate between selected locations, manage simulated oxygen and energy reserves, scan exploration sites, and earn mission scores.

2. How Does It Work?

Our system combines planetary imagery, terrain processing, and graph-based pathfinding.

Step 1 - Data Processing

We use a 6-meter CTX orthorectified mosaic and a corresponding 20-meter Digital Elevation Model (DEM) for the Jezero Crater western fan.

Elevation data is processed to derive terrain slope and create a navigation cost grid. The prototype uses a 267 × 267 grid representing approximately 5.3 × 5.3 kilometers of terrain.

Step 2 - Route Calculation

Users select a starting point and destination on the interactive map.

Our A* pathfinding system calculates two navigation alternatives:

  • Shortest: Prioritizes travel distance while respecting excluded terrain cells.
  • Terrain-aware: Minimizes a modeled travel cost that incorporates terrain slope and distance.

The system prevents paths from crossing cells classified as blocked or unsupported by the dataset.

Step 3 - 3D Exploration

Users can enter a 3D expedition based on the same terrain dataset.

The simulation allows astronauts to explore, follow navigation guidance, recalculate routes, manage limited resources, and scan simulated survey locations.

Mission scores reflect completion, exploration activities, remaining resources, and modeled terrain risks.

3. Technology Stack

MARS NAVIGATOR is developed using:

  • React 18 and TypeScript: Web application architecture and interactive interface.
  • Vite: Frontend development and build system.
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber: Interactive 3D terrain visualization and astronaut expedition.
  • A Pathfinding Algorithm:* Route planning and terrain-weighted navigation.
  • Geospatial Data Processing: Preparing DEM, imagery, slope, and navigation-grid datasets.
  • NASA and USGS Planetary Data: Scientific terrain information and Mars imagery.
  • Cloudflare Pages: Web application hosting.

4. Creativity and Innovation

What makes MARS NAVIGATOR different is the combination of scientific terrain data and an interactive astronaut experience.

Instead of presenting Mars as a static map, we allow users to compare route-planning strategies and experience their consequences through a mission simulation.

The project connects three elements:

  1. Real planetary terrain data.
  2. Explainable navigation decisions.
  3. Interactive learning through exploration.

This makes complex geospatial and pathfinding concepts easier to understand for students, space enthusiasts, and future researchers.

5. Benefits and Intended Impact

MARS NAVIGATOR aims to:

  • Demonstrate how publicly available planetary data can support exploration-planning research.
  • Help users understand the trade-offs between travel distance and terrain difficulty.
  • Encourage interest in planetary science, geospatial technologies, and computational problem-solving.
  • Provide an educational foundation for future Mars-navigation simulations.

Our long-term vision is to develop more advanced exploration scenarios with additional scientific datasets and improved terrain models.

6. Challenges and Limitations

We considered terrain resolution, map alignment, navigation constraints, computational efficiency, and the usability of scientific information.

Our slope-based terrain costs, hazard thresholds, oxygen consumption, and energy consumption are demonstration assumptions. They are not calibrated against actual astronaut operations.

The physical registration between the terrain imagery and elevation data, as well as the DEM's exact vertical reference, also require further validation.

Therefore, MARS NAVIGATOR is an educational and research prototype, not a certified mission-planning or astronaut safety system.
